newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end tad lower on earnings caution.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end tad lower on earnings caution.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed slightly lower in hesitant trading Thursday at the start of the corporate results period, dealers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index dipped 0.1 percent to 117.88, matching broad market losses.
Traders said the market was likely to stay rangebound and cautious Friday ahead of the bulk of company first-quarter earnings announcements.
"Investors would rather keep a low profile until the results come in," one trader said.
However, he noted that the results of electricity sector stocks, likely to be hurt by a recent drought affecting activities at hydro-electric plants, had already been factored into prices.

The country's biggest electricity generator, Endesa, reported first-quarter net gains of 39.8 billion pesos ($95.8 million) Thursday, representing a rise of 18.1 percent compared to the same period of 1996.
"As we expected, Endesa's operational results worsened, while non-operational results improved," one trader said.
Endesa shares gained a modest 1.25 pesos to 257.75.
Session losers beat winners 46 to 31 and 42 stocks closed flat, while volume remained unchanged from Wednesday at 11.9 billion pesos.
Traders said business, like Wednesday, was driven by local players.
Among losers, CBT and Forestal reeled 9.1 percent and 7.6 percent each, while Lansagro, Cementos and Melon fell 5.7 percent, 5.0 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively.
Winners were led by Minera, Somela and Cruz Blanca, which advanced 6.7 percent, 4.3 percent and 4.2 percent, respectively.
